findings.title: Checkpoint-key mesh separation fails for an injected non-default screen and for near-equal meshes
findings.detail: LocalSolvers.l1_key returns 'l1' whenever l1_hmax_mm is None. So LocalSolvers(twin.l1_screen(2.0), l_sub) writes its 2 mm L1 values under the same key as the frozen 4 mm screen, even though the screen carries .hmax_mm = 2.0. The module docstring's promise that 'a workdir never mixes meshes' holds only when the mesh is passed as l1_hmax_mm. Separately, f'{h:g}' keeps 6 significant digits, so 1.9999999 and 2.0 both map to 'l1@2mm'. peec._grid_lines (ceil(diff/hmax - 1e-9)) can mesh those two values differently, so the key can hide a real mesh difference. No current impact: e011_run.py calls local_search with workdir=None.
findings.evidence: Scratch run: LocalSolvers(W.l1_screen(2.0), ...).l1_key == 'l1' while the screen's hmax_mm == 2.0; l1_hmax_mm=1.9999999 -> 'l1@2mm'; 0.1234567 and 0.1234568 -> 'l1@0.123457mm'.
findings.suggested_check: Read getattr(self.l1, 'hmax_mm', self.l1_hmax_mm) in l1_key and format the mesh with repr or more digits.

findings.title: The E011 runner cannot yet use the mesh parameter
findings.detail: experiments/runners/e011_run.py still passes self.M.T._l1 directly to LocalSolvers, proxy_descent, draw_degradations, ablation_random_screen and proxy_alone, and has its own ops.l1 wrapper. So 'the L1 mesh size as a parameter' exists in the library API but cannot be selected from the experiment config without a further runner change. The deliverable is only optimize/local.py, so this limits scope rather than being a defect.
findings.evidence: grep in e011_run.py: lines 180, 256, 262, 270, 280 and 284 inject T._l1.
findings.suggested_check: Add a follow-up runner task that passes l1=None with l1_hmax_mm taken from the config.

findings.title: Coupled retries only move partners in the same direction
findings.detail: Coupled retries move each partner by the same displacement d plus further steps in the same sign. Repairs that trade one parameter against another (one up, the other down) are never offered. I probed all 18 rejected single u-moves at the four 2R end points whose failure is a coupling rule. Four of the in-bound one-partner repairs need the opposite sign (row_HS_u0 against row_HS_gap), and 9 of the 18 rejected moves have no one-partner repair at +-1 or +-2 steps. The docstring states the same-sign rule, so this is a limit of how general the coupled moves are, not a bug.
findings.evidence: Scratch script binds_check.py on the 2R end points (draws 0, 2, 3, 4): 25 in-bound repairs, 0 outside rule_binds, 4 opposite-sign, 9 with no single-partner repair.
findings.suggested_check: If the redesign meant trade-off couplings to be covered, also try opposite-sign partner displacements.

findings.title: Kind label of stuck-search coupled retries differs from the docstring
findings.detail: The module docstring says the move taken by the stuck line search has kind 'line_stuck'. A coupled retry of a rejected line_stuck move is yielded as kind 'coupled', so trajectory and yield statistics attribute it to 'coupled'.
findings.evidence: _Space.checked yields ('coupled', *r) for any kind in _RETRIED, including 'line_stuck'.
findings.suggested_check: Document the behaviour, or tag such retries as line_stuck+coupled.

findings.title: 'Generic' coupled moves are limited to the slot-free-end and die-row rules, on the moved parameter's axis
findings.detail: rule_binds covers slot{i}_free_end and row_{sw}_{u0,v0,gap}. Every other replay rule gets no coupled retry (column inner/outer edges, slot attach, column v edges, feet, landing lines, slot gaps, windows). A v-move that fails a free-end rule because of v-overlap also gets no retry, since the u-axis partners are filtered out. Within the covered rules, my check of rule_binds against derivative._replay found the partner sets correct, and complete for single-partner u repairs.
findings.evidence: Read derivative._replay lines 1120-1245 against rule_binds; probe found 0 repairs with a partner outside rule_binds.

independent_checks_performed: Ran the definition-of-done commands. `uv run pytest -q tests/unit/optimize tests/unit/generate`: 323 passed in 909 s. `uv run ruff check src tests`: all checks passed. `uv run mfos gate --fast`: all gates passed. Also ran test_local_moves.py on its own: 19 passed.

Rebuilt the pre-change package in $TMPDIR from main HEAD's local.py, control.py and twin.py; main's derivative.py and nulls.py are byte-identical to the snapshot. Ran 6 default-config local searches not in the author's tests with both old and new code: a new seed layout, dies_fixed, step_mm=1 with n_joint=3, a 900-eval budget, and the real twin._l1 screen. All digests are identical, and LocalConfig().hash() is bdefe640d8cac683 in both.
Confirmed that LocalSolvers(None, ...) at the default mesh gives the same search digest as injecting twin._l1, and that DEFAULT_HMAX is 4.0e-3 m, so hmax_mm/1000 converts units correctly.

Checked rule_binds by hand against derivative._replay: slot free end, needed/limit, the other columns' facing edges, the split-housing reach, the landing slot's 1 mm clearance, the row_u0 offset, and row_v0 against slot v0/v1 (hts = slot v1 - v0). All partner sets match.

Probed coupling completeness at the four 2R end points: for every rejected single u-move with a coupling-rule failure, tried every other movable u-parameter at +-1 and +-2 steps. 0 valid repairs used a partner outside rule_binds; 4 in-bound repairs needed the opposite sign.
Checked the checkpoint keys: an injected l1_screen(2.0) gets key 'l1', and near-equal meshes share a key under :g formatting.
Read e011_run.py to see how the E011 entry points get their L1 solver.
caveats: Coupled moves cover only the slot-free-end and die-row replay rules. Partners must be on the moved parameter's axis and are displaced in the same direction only.
The L1 mesh parameter is available in twin, control, local and nulls, but the E011 runner still injects twin._l1 directly. Selecting a mesh from the experiment config needs a runner change.
Checkpoint keys keep meshes apart only when the mesh is passed as l1_hmax_mm (not as an injected l1_screen) and only to 6 significant digits.

The default config was confirmed bit-identical to the pre-change code on 6 independent runs with synthetic and real L1 solvers. None of my own runs triggered a perturbation; the author's recorded digest covers that path.
The T0478 task record and research/diagnoses/e011-2r-dev-miss.md are not in this snapshot, so 'completely' was judged against the docstrings and the packet's material.
